target.title: feat: block broad protected-root shell searches
target.body:
Closes #99466
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex/OpenClaw workers could run broad recursive shell searches over high-risk roots such as a home directory, Codex/OpenClaw state, session archives, repo parents, or external workspace roots. On small PR tasks this can turn command output and local session/debug surfaces into oversized live context, making runaway token usage much more likely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a high-confidence exec guard for `rg`, recursive `grep`, and `find` commands in gateway/sandbox execution. The guard reuses OpenClaw's existing command-payload analysis so shell wrappers and command carriers are inspected, blocks only protected-root search shapes, and returns actionable guidance to narrow the path, prefer indexed/search tools, and cap output.

This first pass does not add a user-configurable bypass. It is intentionally scoped to the riskiest broad search shapes from the worker-runaway retro and keeps narrowed repo/task/evidence-path searches allowed.

## User Impact

Agents get an immediate, actionable exec failure instead of walking large protected roots. Narrow searches inside a repo or task directory continue to work, and the exec tool description now teaches the safer default before the command is attempted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts`: 8 passed
  - `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts`: 43 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`
  - 53 passed
- `git diff --check`

Public issue/PR artifacts intentionally avoid raw private transcripts, cookies, endpoint secrets, and full local session logs.
